papers.title: Leaning Over to Reach Far-Away Objects
papers.title_zh: Leaning Over to Reach Far-Away Objects
papers.tldr_zh: We study supported reaching to extend a humanoid robot's wor
papers.cover_zh: We study supported reaching to extend a humanoid robot's wor
papers.abstract_zh: We study supported reaching to extend a humanoid robot's workspace by bracing against the environment for stabilization using a straightforward yet capable whole-body model predictive control (MPC) approach, exclusively with local sensing and fiducial markers. While typical solutions for whole body humanoid control aim at avoiding or accommodating contact, contact is explicitly required to reach objects placed on surfaces far out of normal reach. We employ sampling-based MPC for whole-body leaning, bracing, reaching, and recovery on a Unitree H1-2 humanoid. The controller runs in real-time at 34 Hz on a laptop, transfers sim-to-real, extends reach by about 50 cm beyond the unbraced standing workspace, and sustains the loaded posture for over four minutes, before pose estimation drifts. The controller reaches the commanded target in 89% of trials and completes the full reach-and-recovery cycle in 81%, across 54 trials spanning six targets and three table heights. We further characterize why such a small real-time sampling budget is sufficient, finding that temporal persistence of sampled actions and exploration scale strongly govern success, while CEM provides the widest operating region over planning rate and model mismatch. These results establish a real-world baseline for online, contact-rich humanoid manipulation. Code, videos, and full hardware details are available at https://h12leaner.github.io/

papers.title: WA-JEPA: Goal-Aware Predictive Feedback Action Refinement for a World-Action Model
papers.title_zh: WA-JEPA: Goal-Aware Predictive Feedback Action Refinement for a World-Action Model
papers.tldr_zh: JEPA-based world models predict action consequences in laten
papers.cover_zh: JEPA-based world models predict action consequences in laten
papers.abstract_zh: JEPA-based world models predict action consequences in latent space, but representative planning approaches rely on candidate-action search, requiring repeated evaluation of action sequences and incurring substantial online computational cost. Direct action generation avoids this search, yet how to leverage latent predictions to guide action generation given task goals remains a key challenge in translating learned physical dynamics into effective decisions. We introduce WA-JEPA, a world-action model that couples action generation, action-conditioned latent prediction, and goal-aware feedback. The model first generates an action proposal and predicts the resulting future scenes and proprioceptive states, then refines the proposal through two complementary feedback paths, using the task goal as a reference. Goal-discrepancy residual feedback (GDRF) uses differences between the latent representations of predicted scenes and the task goal to guide chunk-wise action refinement. Future-scene context feedback (FSCF) preserves fine-grained predicted scene representations to guide subsequent action refinement. Jointly learned from offline demonstrations, this process iteratively updates the same plan before execution, making future predictions directly participate in action generation without candidate-action search. We evaluate short-horizon goal reaching, long-horizon tasks, and full-task execution. The results show that goal-aware predictive feedback supports competitive task performance while maintaining a compact model and low online computational cost. Code is available at https://github.com/Dovisya/WA-JEPA.

papers.title: Ego2Sim2Humanoid: Agentic Real-to-Sim for Learning Loco-Manipulation VLAs without Robot Demonstrations
papers.title_zh: Ego2Sim2Humanoid: Agentic Real-to-Sim for Learning Loco-Manipulation VLAs without Robot Demonstrations
papers.tldr_zh: Imitation learning for visuomotor policies typically relies
papers.cover_zh: Imitation learning for visuomotor policies typically relies
papers.abstract_zh: Imitation learning for visuomotor policies typically relies on teleoperated robot demonstrations, which are costly because every episode requires a trained operator controlling a physical robot in real time through teleoperation interfaces and wearable body-tracking hardware. Egocentric glasses capture human demonstrations without a robot or handheld grippers, yet they track only the head and in-view human hands, and directly copying human motion to a robot with different stature, arm reach and hand morphology fails to produce feasible contacts. method{} converts egocentric glasses recordings into physically verified robot training trajectories. An agentic real-to-sim stage reconstructs collision and textured visual assets from the recorded RGB-D and head streams, completes unseen surfaces when needed, and predicts target contact bands on the manipulated objects. During motion adaptation, a grasp planner turns each contact band into a feasible robot wrist pose and finger closure, bilevel stance optimization plans collision-free standing postures that keep hand targets reachable, and a whole-body motion generator synthesizes lower-body locomotion and out-of-view arm motion. Two-stage motion correction then blends visibility transitions kinematically and trains a reinforcement-learning tracking policy in physics simulation under agent-designed semantic rewards, completing manipulation phases even when the object leaves the camera view. Rendering the reconstructed scene through the robot's onboard camera along the optimized rollout yields synchronized robot-view images, proprioception and verified action labels. Fine-tuned exclusively on this converted dataset, without real-robot demonstrations, GR00T N1.7 performed loco-manipulation tasks autonomously on a Unitree G1. Project page: https://robonana.github.io/ego2sim2humanoid/

papers.title: A Unified Control Framework, Mathematical Model, and Five-layer Closed-loop Case Study for Embodied Intelligence Control Systems
papers.title_zh: A Unified Control Framework, Mathematical Model, and Five-layer Closed-loop Case Study for Embodied Intelligence Control Systems
papers.tldr_zh: Embodied intelligence holds that an agent develops cognition
papers.cover_zh: Embodied intelligence holds that an agent develops cognition
papers.abstract_zh: Embodied intelligence holds that an agent develops cognition and behavior through real-time body-environment interaction, so its control system must tightly couple perception, decision making, learning, optimization, constraints, and physical execution. This report asks whether a unified framework exists, how its mathematical models unify, and how the framework is realized computably. Four conclusions emerge. (1) No single framework is accepted, but the field converges on a common skeleton: from operational-space and whole-body control to MPC, reinforcement learning, active inference, and diffusion/flow policies, all reduce to constrained sequential decision making on the configuration manifold. (2) Two languages describe it-deterministic optimal control (Euler-Lagrange plus constrained OCP, reduced in real time to a QP) and probabilistic inference (MDP/POMDP plus free-energy minimization)-rigorously bridged by control as inference and KL/path-integral control. (3) Engineering unification is already achieved by constrained optimization; the new frontier is cross-morphology, cross-task shared representation. (4) The hardest gap is provable stability and safety, the entry point for spectral, geometric, differentiable-optimization, and safe-learning methods. A single-link manipulator then runs through all five layers: L4 parses the instruction into a reference, L3 identifies a Koopman lifted linear world model, L2 solves a receding constrained QP, L1 adds torque saturation and a CBF, and L0 is the true nonlinear plant. Closed-loop tracking RMSE is 0.0218 rad with all constraints satisfied and a world-model error near 5 x 10^-6 rad, reported with curves and a 3D animation.

papers.title: Refinement vs. Replanning: Inference Compute Allocation in Robot Policies
papers.title_zh: Refinement vs. Replanning: Inference Compute Allocation in Robot Policies
papers.tldr_zh: A frozen chunked robot policy can spend deployment-time infe
papers.cover_zh: A frozen chunked robot policy can spend deployment-time infe
papers.abstract_zh: A frozen chunked robot policy can spend deployment-time inference compute in two coupled ways: more work within each policy call to refine a predicted action chunk, or more frequent policy calls to replan from fresh observations. We study this allocation without updating model weights. Our evaluation procedure reports success with both nominal compute rate and complete attempt cost, selects comparisons on discovery tasks, and tests prespecified comparisons on held-out tasks. Comparisons added after inspecting the held-out results only summarize observed patterns. We demonstrate the procedure with one frozen SmolVLA checkpoint in synchronous LIBERO simulation, using denoising count as the refinement control and fixing chunk length at K=50. Arithmetic and latency characterize cost differently: at d=10, 82.1% of counted arithmetic is independent of denoising, whereas a descriptive affine fit to fixed-input host time assigns 17.7% to its intercept. At h=2, d=2 succeeds on 139/160 attempts versus 122/160 for d=5 (+10.6 percentage points; task-conditional 95% interval: +4.4 to +16.9), while using 5.9% less arithmetic per control step. Executing h=5 rather than h=2 at d=2 yields 138/160 versus 139/160 successes and 60.7% lower arithmetic per attempt; equivalence is not established. The case study shows why deployment adaptation must evaluate generation effort and feedback frequency jointly; it does not define a universal setting.

papers.title: LogT: Logically Think with Images for Visual Search
papers.title_zh: LogT: Logically Think with Images for Visual Search
papers.tldr_zh: Thinking with images empowers vision-language models (VLMs)
papers.cover_zh: Thinking with images empowers vision-language models (VLMs)
papers.abstract_zh: Thinking with images empowers vision-language models (VLMs) to use an external Zoom-in tool for fine-grained visual search. Recent works employ supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) with tool-specific designs to enable such capabilities. However, achieving logical reasoning alongside accurate and efficient tool use remains a significant challenge. To address this, we shift the focus away from increasing RL complexity and instead identify SFT data quality as a key bottleneck. We then propose LogT (short for Logically Think with Images), a fully automated SFT data engine that explicitly enforces logic-chain-guided reasoning. LogT generates an SFT dataset featuring challenging, visually grounded questions and structured tool-use traces with human-like logic. We validate our approach by fine-tuning two base models, Qwen2.5-VL-7B and InternVL3.5-8B, on the dataset and evaluating them across seven benchmark test sets. We show that LogT-SFT based on Qwen2.5-VL-7B outperforms the state-of-the-art trained with both SFT and RL, despite using 3.1$×$ less data and $>120×$ fewer GPU hours. Furthermore, applying a simple RL recipe without tool-specific design on LogT-SFT yields a model that surpasses prior methods with complex RL setups by a substantial 9.59-point margin. In addition to strong performance gains, our model exhibits higher tool-use accuracy and efficiency, as well as more structured and logically consistent reasoning traces, directly validating the effectiveness of our approach.

papers.title: Wireless Edge-Assisted Adaptive Latent Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models in Physical AI
papers.title_zh: Wireless Edge-Assisted Adaptive Latent Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models in Physical AI
papers.abstract_zh: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable embodied artificial intelligence (AI) by translating visual observations and language instructions into robotic actions. Emerging use cases in physical AI are expected to drive the need for efficient inference and communication, as the computational demands of the VLA models pose challenges for real-time control with limited onboard resources. Test-time scaling through latent reasoning allows these models to refine hidden representations without generating explicit chain-of-thought (CoT) tokens, but introduces a trade-off between task success, inference latency, and energy consumption. In this paper, we address the efficient collaborative inference under a realistic communication scenario. We propose a wireless edge-assisted framework for adaptive latent reasoning (WEALR) that augments onboard computation with edge computing. A decision-making agent jointly selects the execution location and latent-reasoning convergence threshold. We formulate this joint adaptation as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP). A Lagrangian-constrained deep reinforcement learning (CDRL) approach, namely trust region policy optimization Lagrangian (TRPO-Lag), learns to balance task performance and resource consumption under varying wireless conditions and task requirements. We evaluate the framework using LIBERO manipulation tasks, profiled VLA inference costs, and ray-traced wireless channels. Experimental results demonstrate that TRPO-Lag achieves up to 23% higher feasibility-weighted task success rate compared to benchmark CDRL methods.

papers.title: Self-Calibrating Vision-Agent-Action: Deploying Pick-and-Place to New Robot Cells without Demonstrations or Fine-Tuning
papers.title_zh: Self-Calibrating Vision-Agent-Action: Deploying Pick-and-Place to New Robot Cells without Demonstrations or Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract_zh: In simulation, Vision-Agent-Action (VAA) performs pick-and-place in robot cells with gripper or base-frame changes without robot demonstrations or fine-tuning. It uses pre-trained vision-language and language models for interpretation, measures the command map and camera geometry from its own motion and fingertips, estimates lens distortion, and plans grasps from measured object depth. A controlled study of eight public LIBERO-fine-tuned vision-language-action models (VLAs) varies robot hardware, camera geometry, appearance, and base frame. Gripper and frame changes dominate their losses in the tested fractional design. Across 18 cells with these changes, frozen VAA achieves 230/360 successes (64%), the refined VAA 268/360 (74%), and the strongest released VLA on this subset 76/360 (21%). Paired ablations support the self-calibration bundle, lens estimation under compounded changes, and the measured-depth pipeline. On a two-step LIBERO-Goal chain with object state carried between instructions, VAA completes 54/60 chains in changed cells, while four evaluated VLAs complete none.

papers.title: RoboCoEvo: Expanding Robot Capabilities through Agent-Policy Co-Evolution
papers.title_zh: RoboCoEvo: Expanding Robot Capabilities through Agent-Policy Co-Evolution
papers.tldr_zh: Integrating MLLM-based agents with robotic foundation models
papers.cover_zh: Integrating MLLM-based agents with robotic foundation models
papers.abstract_zh: Integrating MLLM-based agents with robotic foundation models has attracted increasing attention as a means of enhancing robotic capabilities. However, the improvement of such integrated systems remains largely decoupled across their agent and model components, with advances in one component not necessarily benefiting the other, substantially limiting the capabilities of the combined system. As both MLLMs and robotic foundation models become increasingly capable, fully realizing their combined potential calls for co-evolution, an iterative process in which improvements in agents and robotic foundation models reinforce one another. We propose RoboCoEvo, a failure-guided co-evolution framework that couples the refinement of the agent's explicit and reusable executable knowledge with parameter learning in robotic foundation models, such as vision-language-action (VLA) models. Through a code-as-policy formulation, the agent develops and refines executable failure-detection and recovery programs, generating targeted corrective experience. Post-training consolidates the resulting corrective behaviors into the robotic model's end-to-end policy, improving autonomous task execution. Changes in the updated policy's failure distribution, in turn, guide subsequent revisions to the agent's programs. Experiments on BEHAVIOR-1K, RoboCasa, and RoboTwin demonstrate sustained improvements in autonomous VLA task performance across successive co-evolution rounds.

papers.title: ImpedanceMimic: Learned Impedance as Action Space for Force-Accurate Motion Imitation
papers.title_zh: ImpedanceMimic: Learned Impedance as Action Space for Force-Accurate Motion Imitation
papers.tldr_zh: Recovering the forces behind a motion is ill-posed: differen
papers.cover_zh: Recovering the forces behind a motion is ill-posed: differen
papers.abstract_zh: Recovering the forces behind a motion is ill-posed: different controllers can reproduce the same movement while generating different contact forces. Physics-based motion imitation resolves this ambiguity through simulation, but relies on fixed-gain proportional-derivative (PD) control. We show that fixed gains impose a trade-off between motion and force tracking, as contact and swing place conflicting demands on joint stiffness and damping. We introduce ImpedanceMimic, a reinforcement-learning policy that modulates per-joint stiffness, damping, and position setpoints from motion and force measurements, but requires only motion at inference. Across 129 participants and six activities, ImpedanceMimic outperforms matched fixed-gain PD under every integration scheme, direct-torque, muscle-actuated and existing imitation controllers in kinematic and force fidelity, approaching a dedicated motion-to-force regressor. By expressing gains as multiples of inertia-scaled priors, a single policy controls subject-specific biomechanical models without explicit anthropometric input and transfers zero-shot to unseen humans and a humanoid robot. The learned impedance forms a low-dimensional representation of motor state, shared across bodies, that generalizes to withheld activities: stiffness scales with load, and damping anticipates unloading.

papers.title: Residual Reinforcement Learning for Visual Servo Control with Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer
papers.title_zh: Residual Reinforcement Learning for Visual Servo Control with Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer
papers.tldr_zh: We address tracking a moving object on a conveyor with a Fra
papers.cover_zh: We address tracking a moving object on a conveyor with a Fra
papers.abstract_zh: We address tracking a moving object on a conveyor with a Franka Emika Panda robot arm, despite an imprecise digital twin, measurement errors, and noise. Our novel approach augments a loop-shaped inverse-Jacobian PI controller with a residual policy learned via Soft Actor-Critic in the digital twin. A delay-compensated Kalman filter fuses out-of-sequence camera measurements to provide latency-aware moving target position estimates. We compare the achieved performance to a performance bound for a class of model-based controllers derived from a frequency-domain sensitivity analysis, quantifying the minimum achievable error imposed by uncertain kinematic model mismatch. Simulation and hardware experiments indicate that our residual policy drives tracking error below the bound. Across conveyor speeds (27.9-41.8 mm/s), our method reduces mean tracking errors from 1.1-1.4 mm (baseline inverse-Jacobian PI) to 0.3-0.7 mm. These results show that learning residual corrections in a limited-fidelity simulator, combined with delay compensation, can substantially improve model-based control under modeling and measurement uncertainties while maintaining reliable sim-to-real transfer.

papers.title: Certify, Then Select: Viability-Aware Runtime Steering of Frozen Diffusion Policies
papers.title_zh: Certify, Then Select: Viability-Aware Runtime Steering of Frozen Diffusion Policies
papers.tldr_zh: Diffusion policies, which generate short action sequences by
papers.cover_zh: Diffusion policies, which generate short action sequences by
papers.abstract_zh: Diffusion policies, which generate short action sequences by denoising random noise, are a leading way to learn robot skills from demonstrations. Once deployed, they meet constraints the demonstrations never contained, and retraining for each is impractical. A safety filter edits the policy's action to satisfy them, but the edit ignores the task, and a large edit can leave the policy where it cannot continue. We propose CAST (Certified Action Selection at Test time): draw a few action chunks from the frozen policy, certify each with a barrier condition, and execute the certified chunk that a learned value ensemble ranks highest. We prove that a certified step is safe whatever the critic does; that, whenever a certified sample exists, the executed chunk stays within log N nats of the policy conditioned on feasibility, while a safety-filter projection can be singular to it; and that an exact closed-loop identity splits the gain of ranking into availability, spread and the critic's target. Certifying the next chunk is not enough: a generative controller can have safe actions available now and none later. We characterise the safe control authority of a frozen policy under finite sampling, and CAST-V preserves it through a policy-conditioned viability, estimated with a model under a finite-sample guarantee or learned from the controller's own logs (CAST-VL). On robomimic manipulation, a planar quadrotor, a MuJoCo humanoid and a unicycle, with frozen policies, CAST raises joint task-and-constraint success above the output filter in nearly every setting; certifying before ranking is decisive where a filter's edit is large, and viability removes most dead ends that one-step certification cannot see. Project page: https://clmoro.github.io/cast.

papers.title: ST-GAT: A Leakage-Free Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Framework for Robust Network Intrusion Detection
papers.title_zh: ST-GAT: A Leakage-Free Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Framework for Robust Network Intrusion Detection
papers.tldr_zh: Intrusion detection systems are a central defence in modern
papers.cover_zh: Intrusion detection systems are a central defence in modern
papers.abstract_zh: Intrusion detection systems are a central defence in modern networks. Deep learning models report strong anomaly-detection results, but evaluations on standard benchmarks such as CSE-CIC-IDS-2018 are often inflated by two methodological problems: temporal leakage from overlapping sliding windows, and contamination from preprocessing fitted before the train/test split. Per-flow classifiers also ignore the spatio-temporal dependencies across sequences of network flows. We propose a Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Network (ST-GAT) that represents traffic as a sequence of graph snapshots. It builds k-Nearest Neighbour (k-NN) edges within each window, applies multi-head Graph Attention Network (GAT) layers for spatial aggregation, and uses a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network with temporal attention for sequence modelling. To prevent leakage, we use non-overlapping temporal windows (stride equal to window length) and fit all preprocessing on the training split only. We compare three class-imbalance strategies: inverse class-frequency weighting, dynamic balanced sampling, and few-shot metric prototyping. Across three random seeds, ST-GAT with inverse class weighting reached a Macro-F1 of 96.65% (+/- 0.87) and an accuracy of 99.14%. This is 14.3 percentage points higher in Macro-F1 than a per-flow Random Forest baseline (82.34%). Balanced sampling reduced Macro-F1 by 2.3 points (to 94.37%) relative to loss weighting. This suggests that aggressive resampling of small, noisy minority classes can hurt detection in heavily imbalanced traffic.

papers.title: DecoEdit: Beyond Flat Control for 3D-Aware Unified Image Editing
papers.title_zh: DecoEdit: Beyond Flat Control for 3D-Aware Unified Image Editing
papers.tldr_zh: While recent advances in multimodal image editing have achie
papers.cover_zh: While recent advances in multimodal image editing have achie
papers.abstract_zh: While recent advances in multimodal image editing have achieved impressive results, current frameworks remain largely confined to ``flat" 2D controls (e.g., text prompts, bounding boxes, or masks). Precise 3D-aware geometric manipulation -- such as coordinating an object's location, physical scale, and 3D orientation while strictly preserving its fine-grained identity -- remains an elusive challenge, typically suffering from severe detail degradation or requiring expensive per-instance fine-tuning. In this paper, we present DecoEdit, an all-in-one image editing framework that goes beyond flat control by seamlessly integrating 1D textual, 2D spatial, and 3D volumetric inputs under a unified architecture. First, to power this unified model, we establish a data curation pipeline and curate a large-scale dataset, namely DecoDataset, containing 1.6 million samples, encompassing diverse multi-dimensional (1D/2D/3D) tasks and their complex compositions. Furthermore, we establish a comprehensive image editing benchmark named DecoBench to systematically evaluate multi-task editing performance. Finally, to address the fundamental trade-off between complex spatial transformations and identity preservation, we propose a novel decoupled pipeline: DecoEdit factorizes the editing process by utilizing structural guidance from SAM-3D to anchor the target geometry, scale, and spatial orientation, while concurrently leveraging a detail-preservation path to lock in high-fidelity textures. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DecoEdit achieves state-of-the-art results. Notably, on the challenging 3D spatial pose and orientation control tasks, DecoEdit significantly outperforms leading closed-source models such as Seedream 5.0 in both geometric accuracy and identity consistency.

papers.title: SuperGlance: Driving at a Glance with a Vision-Language Model
papers.title_zh: SuperGlance: Driving at a Glance with a Vision-Language Model
papers.tldr_zh: Autonomous driving is turning to vision-language-action mode
papers.cover_zh: Autonomous driving is turning to vision-language-action mode
papers.abstract_zh: Autonomous driving is turning to vision-language-action models (VLAs). They answer and plan by decoding, one step at a time. Each step is another forward pass, so a plan can take over a second of GPU time. Embodied AI often pairs such a slow, reasoning System 2 with a fast System 1 that acts. Human drivers plan at a glance, with System 1. Faster designs usually put System 1 outside the vision-language model (VLM), in a planner without its abilities. Yet before a VLM writes its first token, it has already read the scene into one hidden state. We show that, once trained, this hidden state is enough to drive and to answer questions about what the model sees. SuperGlance reads it to turn a decoder-only VLM into an encoder-style driving policy. Its linear head scores a fixed set of 5,273 candidate trajectories. With the set fixed, rewards are computed offline, so supervised targets can be reward-weighted and reinforcement learning maximizes the exact expected reward. Before and during policy training, multiple-choice training keeps the VLM's visual abilities in one pass, so the policy still answers questions about driving scenes. Training questions are built against shortcuts. Each must be answered right in two option orders. Against drift, a KL term keeps each stage near its starting model. One pass offers VLAs a more plausible path to System 1. SuperGlance answers visual multiple-choice questions as well as its base VLM does by decoding. It plans in 84 ms of GPU time, six times faster than Qwen-Drive-1.0, and at least as well on NAVSIM, PAI-AV and WOD-E2E. In AlpaSim closed loop, km per at-fault incident holds for both planners up to a 300-ms delay and drops beyond. With GPU time charged as delay, SuperGlance's lead over Qwen-Drive-1.0 grows from 2.8 to 3.9 times. Delayed by 1.2 s, our model falls below Qwen-Drive-1.0 at its own 518 ms.
